edges.description: Valproate inhibits HDAC1 at concentrations in the therapeutic range, so the enzyme is engaged directly by the drug that reaches the embryo.
edges.source: Transplacental Valproate Exposure of the Embryo

edges.description: Valproate binds the high-affinity folate receptors noncompetitively, which is a second drug-target interaction alongside the HDAC one. Calling the two branches parallel is a statement about how they are curated, not a claim that they are independent: valproate also lowers placental expression of folate carriers and one-carbon enzymes, which would make the folate lesion partly downstream of the transcriptional one. Both routes are recorded here and neither is ranked.
edges.source: Transplacental Valproate Exposure of the Embryo

edges.description: Exposed embryos shift transiently to a more oxidising glutathione redox potential. Marked indirect because no step is established between the drug and the redox change itself.
edges.source: Transplacental Valproate Exposure of the Embryo

edges.description: Removing deacetylase activity leaves histones hyperacetylated and derepresses transcription, which is the immediate consequence of the inhibition.
edges.target: Embryonic Histone Hyperacetylation and Ectopic Transcription

edges.description: In human neural progenitors the same exposure that remodels chromatin shifts the cells out of the cycle toward differentiation, with the closed regions enriched for proliferative transcription-factor motifs and the opened ones for neuronal differentiation. The cited experiment measures both changes under one exposure rather than showing that the first causes the second, and transcription necessarily intervenes, so the link is recorded as indirect with unknown intermediates.
edges.source: Embryonic Histone Hyperacetylation and Ectopic Transcription
edges.target: Altered Neural Progenitor Proliferation and Differentiation

edges.description: Exposure misplaces Hoxa2 expression and lowers Sox9 in the premigratory cranial crest. The transcriptional misregulation is consistent with the chromatin lesion, but no cited experiment connects the acetylation mark to these specific genes, so the intermediates are unknown.
edges.source: Embryonic Histone Hyperacetylation and Ectopic Transcription
edges.target: Disturbed Cranial Neural Crest Formation and Migration

edges.description: Exposed neuroepithelium induces senescence through p19Arf. The route from chromatin state to p19Arf induction is not established in the cited work.
edges.source: Embryonic Histone Hyperacetylation and Ectopic Transcription

edges.description: Cell-cell junction genes and proteins change in exposed human spinal cord organoids. The link to the chromatin lesion is inferred from the exposure being the same, not demonstrated.
edges.source: Embryonic Histone Hyperacetylation and Ectopic Transcription

edges.description: In human neurons the drug's HDAC and GSK-3 inhibition downregulates dendritic genes including MARCKSL1, which is named as the mediator — so an intermediate is identified rather than merely postulated.
edges.source: Embryonic Histone Hyperacetylation and Ectopic Transcription
edges.target: Impaired Dendritic Morphogenesis and Synapse Maturation

edges.description: Reduced folate uptake is taken to produce the embryonic metabolite shift. The receptor work is in a kidney-derived cell line and the metabolite work in mouse embryos, so no single experiment connects them; the authors of the receptor study state the link conditionally themselves.

Lower folate availability during neurulation is proposed to cause closure failure. The steps between the metabolite shift and the tissue failure are not established, and the human supplementation evidence does not confirm the route, so this edge is deliberately weak.

Pretreatment with an NRF2 inducer prevents both the redox shift and a substantial part of the closure failure, which is the strongest argument that the redox change is on the causal path rather than beside it.

Apical constriction is the cell behaviour that bends the neural plate, so its impairment is a mechanical account of closure failure, with the intervening step — neural plate bending — identified rather than unknown. Not marked direct because the cited evidence is a hedged inference from lumen size in a brain organoid in which no neural tube either closed or failed to close.
The human lesion closure failure produces, characteristically lumbosacral.

The affected crest populations are the ones that migrate to the frontonasal mass and first branchial arch, which is where the face is built. The step to the facial gestalt is this entry's inference and not the authors': the outcomes they name for this mechanism are trigeminal axonal elongation and reduced head size, and reduced head size is something this entry records as not established in humans. The edge is therefore marked indirect with unknown intermediates rather than direct.
edges.source: Disturbed Cranial Neural Crest Formation and Migration

edges.description: One of the facial features the consensus statement enumerates as the gestalt this dysmorphogenesis produces.
One of the facial features the consensus statement enumerates as the gestalt this dysmorphogenesis produces.

One of the facial features the consensus statement's diagnostic criteria enumerate for this gestalt.
The severe end of the metopic continuum, where the ridging has become suture fusion.
Premature suture fusion, metopic in the reported cases.
Palatal shelf fusion fails. Curated as a consequence of this node because the affected crest streams build the first branchial arch, from which the palate derives.
Whichever direction the balance shifts, the cortex is built from the wrong number of cells at the wrong time; the mouse work states the outcome as neocortical dysgenesis.
edges.source: Altered Neural Progenitor Proliferation and Differentiation

edges.description: Senescent neuroepithelial cells are permanently arrested, and the paper locates them in tissue where neurogenesis is already defective.
Dendrites and synapses are the substrate of circuits, and the protein named here is described as essential for exactly those processes.
edges.source: Impaired Dendritic Morphogenesis and Synapse Maturation

edges.description: Building the cortex and cerebellum with the wrong cell numbers and laminar distribution is taken to alter the circuits they form. This edge carries no evidence of its own on purpose: no cited experiment follows a specific cytoarchitectural change through to a circuit measurement, and the one sentence that might have been used here — that the rat cerebellar findings parallel human autism neuropathology — is a cross-species validity remark about Purkinje counts, not a statement about this step. It is attached to the source node instead.

The step from altered circuits to measured cognition and behaviour. It carries no evidence because none exists in the cited literature: the human evidence for the outcome is epidemiological, and the mechanistic evidence stops at the cellular and tissue level. The edge is asserted as the entry's inference and labelled as such.
The commonest outcome, and the one that occurs without any structural malformation.
The severe end of the cognitive distribution.
The earliest-presenting feature, and the one MONDO singles out.
The persisting form of the verbal deficit.
The neurodevelopmental diagnosis most strongly associated with the exposure.
Raised specifically by valproate among antiseizure medications.
Gross and fine motor delay accompany the cognitive picture.
The educational consequence of the cognitive profile.
One of the domains measured below expectation in both cohorts.
Maternal dosing delivers the drug to the embryo directly, at fetal concentrations exceeding maternal ones, which is the initiating step of every branch curated here.
edges.target: Transplacental Valproate Exposure of the Embryo

edges.description: Supplementation is directed at the folate branch, and the animal rescue experiments act on it, but the human evidence does not establish that the observed protection runs through this node rather than through folate-dependent processes generally. Attached to this node rather than to the shared downstream outcome because it is the branch the intervention targets.
Co-medication raises the observed malformation rate, but the same analysis attributes the increase primarily to valproate dose, so no mechanism is asserted for the combination itself.
edges.target: Transplacental Valproate Exposure of the Embryo
Transplacental Valproate Exposure of the Embryo

edges.description: Measures the chromatin response directly in human cells, and finds it is not the simple opening that HDAC inhibition alone would predict.
edges.limitations: A single cell type and a 48-hour acute exposure, which the authors state does not model chronic clinical administration. Chromatin accessibility is not histone acetylation, so the mark itself is inferred rather than measured.
edges.source: Genotyped human neural progenitor population exposed to valproic acid
edges.target: Embryonic Histone Hyperacetylation and Ectopic Transcription

edges.description: The proliferation reduction is present in every donor at 1 mM, so it is a property of the exposure rather than of a susceptible subset.
edges.limitations: Proliferation in dissociated culture is not neurogenesis in a developing cortex, and the direction conflicts with what mouse cortex shows in vivo.
edges.source: Genotyped human neural progenitor population exposed to valproic acid
edges.target: Altered Neural Progenitor Proliferation and Differentiation

edges.description: Identifies the junctional programme as the thing that changes, in human tissue, during the process that fails.
edges.limitations: Organoids lack the surrounding mesoderm, surface ectoderm and mechanical environment that contribute to closure in vivo, and no axial patterning establishes that the lumbosacral level is the one modelled.
edges.source: Human spinal cord organoid model of valproate-induced neurulation failure

edges.description: Measures apical constriction directly, by lumen size, and shows a teratogenic and a genetic cause of neural tube defects converging on it.
edges.limitations: The spheroids have no dorsoventral or rostrocaudal patterning, so the model cannot speak to the axial level at which the human defect occurs — which is the central limitation for this disease, whose characteristic lesion is lumbosacral. Lumen size is a proxy for a cell behaviour rather than a measurement of closure: no neural tube either closes or fails to close in this system.
edges.source: Human single-rosette brain organoid model of apical constriction failure

edges.description: Shows the progenitor deficit in a human three-dimensional system and localizes it to the subtype that expands the human cortex.
edges.limitations: Organoids are immature, lack vasculature, microglia and long-range inputs, and have no behavioural readout. The Wnt/beta-catenin involvement reported here is an association within the model, not a demonstrated requirement in vivo.
edges.source: Human dorsal forebrain organoid model of outer radial glia depletion
edges.target: Altered Neural Progenitor Proliferation and Differentiation

edges.description: Establishes the developmental restriction by direct comparison of immature and mature neurons in the same system.
edges.limitations: Directly reprogrammed neurons mature on an accelerated, artificial schedule that may not map onto fetal timing, and single cultured neurons lack the circuit context in which dendritic deficits would produce a phenotype.
edges.source: Directly reprogrammed human neurons with staged valproate exposure
edges.target: Impaired Dendritic Morphogenesis and Synapse Maturation

edges.description: Reproduces the behavioural end of the neurodevelopmental arm, including the sensory abnormalities that the human cohort data put at 80% of diagnosed individuals. Pointed at the organism-scale outcome node rather than at circuit formation, because what this model observes is behaviour.
edges.limitations: A single high intraperitoneal bolus at one developmental moment is not the continuous, variable oral exposure of a human pregnancy, and the model was built and validated against idiopathic autism rather than against fetal valproate syndrome. It says nothing about the malformation arm, and the behaviours scored are rodent analogues of human constructs.
edges.source: Prenatal valproate rat model of autism

edges.description: The same exposure and timing reduce Purkinje cell number in the cerebellar vermis, with the posterior lobe affected more than the anterior — a regional gradient rather than a global loss.
edges.limitations: The human comparison is autism neuropathology, not neuropathology from individuals with fetal valproate syndrome, so the parallel is to a related condition.
edges.source: Prenatal valproate rat model of autism

edges.description: Tests the folate branch by varying one-carbon capacity genetically instead of varying the drug, which is the more informative direction.
edges.limitations: A single 400 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at E7.5, and the readout is malformation rate rather than a measurement of folate status in the embryo. The human association is with the mother's genotype; in the mouse, dam and fetus share it, so the experiment cannot separate maternal from fetal contribution.
edges.source: Mthfr 677C>T knock-in mouse with valproate exposure

edges.description: Intervening on the antioxidant response, not on the drug, reduces both the redox shift and the defect.
edges.limitations: The mouse defect is exencephaly, a cranial failure, while the characteristic human lesion is lumbosacral spina bifida, so the axial level differs. D3T induces a broad transcriptional programme, so the rescue is not specific to glutathione redox state. The two halves of the result also come from different preparations: the redox measurement from CD-1 whole-embryo culture with valproate applied in vitro, and the defect rescue from C57BL/6J dams dosed in utero, so no single experiment shows both in one strain and system.
edges.source: Mouse neural tube defect model with NRF2 induction

edges.description: Shows both halves of the node — reduced crest formation at midbrain-rhombomere 1/2 and misrouted rhombomere 4 crest carrying the wrong positional identity.
edges.limitations: Embryonic readouts over hours to days, with no follow-through to a formed face, so the connection to the human gestalt is inferred. Rat and human craniofacial development differ in the relative contribution of the frontonasal mass.
edges.source: Rat cranial neural crest exposure model
edges.target: Disturbed Cranial Neural Crest Formation and Migration

nodes.description: Circuits assembled from disordered neurogenesis and from neurons whose dendrites and synapses matured abnormally. This node is the circuit-level step only; the clinical consequence is the separate organism-scale node below, because no cited experiment follows a circuit measurement through to a cognitive score and bundling the two would hide that gap.

evidence.reference_title: Assessing molecular gene by treatment interactions using a population of neural progenitors exposed to valproic acid and lithium.
evidence.snippet: Gene regulatory responses to valproic acid (VPA), which is also a prenatal risk factor for autism, and lithium were highly enriched in genetic risk for psychiatric disorders, demonstrating the convergence of environmental and genetic factors.

nodes.description: Exposure changes the balance between progenitor self-renewal and differentiation, and the direction of the change is not consistent across systems. Human neural progenitors from 83 donors and human forebrain organoids both lose proliferative capacity; rat cortical progenitors differentiate prematurely through a beta-catenin-Ras-ERK-p21 route; but mouse cortex in vivo shows the opposite, with progenitors failing to exit the cycle on schedule. The node is curated as a disturbance of the balance rather than as a direction, and the disagreement is carried in the attached evidence and in a discussion.
nodes.id: Altered Neural Progenitor Proliferation and Differentiation

evidence.reference_title: Assessing molecular gene by treatment interactions using a population of neural progenitors exposed to valproic acid and lithium.
evidence.snippet: VPA exposure leads to consistent reductions in proliferation across all donors at clinically relevant concentrations

evidence.reference_title: Valproic acid exposure decreases neurogenic potential of outer radial glia in human brain organoids.
evidence.snippet: We found that VPA exposure in organoids caused a reduction in the size and impairment in the proliferation and expansion of neural progenitor cells (NPCs) in a dose-dependent manner.

evidence.reference_title: Valproic acid induces differentiation and inhibition of proliferation in neural progenitor cells via the beta-catenin-Ras-ERK-p21Cip/WAF1 pathway.
evidence.snippet: We report here that 1 mM VPA simultaneously induces differentiation and reduces proliferation of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF)-treated embryonic day 14 (E14) rat cerebral cortex neural progenitor cells (NPCs).

evidence.reference_title: In Utero Exposure to Valproic Acid Induces Neocortical Dysgenesis via Dysregulation of Neural Progenitor Cell Proliferation/Differentiation.
evidence.snippet: We show that VPA decreases the probability of differentiation of the neural progenitor cells (NPCs) in mice, resulting in an abnormally increased number of projection neurons in the superficial layers of the neocortex.

experimental_models.description: The proliferation reduction is present in every donor at 1 mM, so it is a property of the exposure rather than of a susceptible subset.
experimental_models.name: Genotyped human neural progenitor population exposed to valproic acid

experimental_models.description: Shows the progenitor deficit in a human three-dimensional system and localizes it to the subtype that expands the human cortex.
experimental_models.name: Human dorsal forebrain organoid model of outer radial glia depletion

nodes.description: Forward-facing nostrils, curated separately from the short nose they accompany.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of individuals with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder; a consensus statement from the European Reference Network for Congenital Malformations and Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: short nose with forward-facing (anteverted) nostrils

nodes.description: Valproate combined with another antiseizure medication. Recorded as modulating rather than exacerbating, because the EURAP analysis found the malformation rate tracked valproate dose rather than the combination: polytherapy marks higher risk without being shown to add risk of its own, and nothing cited claims co-medication increases placental valproate transfer.

evidence.reference_title: Dose-dependent teratogenicity of valproate in mono- and polytherapy: an observational study.
evidence.snippet: The frequency of MCMs at 1 year after birth was 10.0% for VPA monotherapy, 11.3% for exposures to VPA and LTG, and 11.7% for exposures to VPA + another (non-LTG) AED.

nodes.description: ADHD at an absolute 15-year risk of 11% after exposure against 4.6% unexposed. The relative increase is modest beside the autism signal, and the Danish cohort found it for valproate and not for other antiepileptic drugs.

evidence.reference_title: Association of Prenatal Exposure to Valproate and Other Antiepileptic Drugs With Risk for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Offspring.
evidence.snippet: The absolute 15-year risk of ADHD was 4.6% (95% CI, 4.5%-4.6%) in children unexposed to valproate and 11.0% (95% CI, 8.2%-14.2%) in children who were exposed to valproate in pregnancy.

evidence.reference_title: Association of Prenatal Exposure to Valproate and Other Antiepileptic Drugs With Risk for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Offspring.
evidence.snippet: No associations were found between other AEDs and ADHD.

nodes.description: Autism is the neurodevelopmental diagnosis most strongly associated with the exposure: 2.7% to 10.5% of exposed children in population cohorts, 6-15% of exposed individuals by the consensus statement's reckoning, a threefold pooled hazard overall and sixfold above 1 g/day, and 62.9% among individuals who already carry a clinical diagnosis. The frequency band follows the population denominator; the diagnosed-cohort figure is far higher because that cohort is selected on being affected. The presentation is reported to differ from idiopathic autism in having an even sex ratio and no regression.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of individuals with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder; a consensus statement from the European Reference Network for Congenital Malformations and Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: The prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is 6–15% in VPA exposed individuals

evidence.reference_title: Gestational Exposure to Valproate and Autism Spectrum Disorder or Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Offspring: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: Gestational exposure to valproate was associated with an increased risk of ASD and ADHD; the risks for ASD were greater at doses ≥ 1000 mg/day.

evidence.reference_title: Gestational Exposure to Valproate and Autism Spectrum Disorder or Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Offspring: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: Notably, anytime gestational exposure to high-dose valproate (> 1.0 to 1.1 g/day) was associated with a substantially elevated risk of ASD (aHR, 6.32; 95% CI, 3.12-12.80, N = 1,719,825).

evidence.reference_title: Characteristics of fetal anticonvulsant syndrome associated autistic disorder.
evidence.snippet: Fetal anticonvulsant syndrome associated autistic disorder is characterized by an even sex ratio, absence of regression or skill loss, and language delay in the absence of global delay.

evidence.reference_title: Association of Prenatal Exposure to Antiseizure Medication With Risk of Autism and Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: In same-aged children of mothers with epilepsy exposed to topiramate and valproate monotherapy, 4.3% and 2.7%, respectively, had ASD, and 3.1% and 2.4% had ID.

evidence.reference_title: Risk of Autism after Prenatal Topiramate, Valproate, or Lamotrigine Exposure.
evidence.snippet: With restriction to children born to mothers with epilepsy, the incidence was 4.2% with no exposure to antiseizure medication (8815 children), 6.2% with exposure to topiramate (1030 children), 10.5% with exposure to valproate (800 children), and 4.1% with exposure to lamotrigine (4205 children).

evidence.reference_title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes in children and adults with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder: A contribution from the ConcePTION project.
evidence.snippet: Rates of neurodevelopmental disorders, particularly autistic spectrum disorders (62.9%) and sensory problems (80.6%) are particularly central to the FVSD phenotype.

nodes.description: The only intervention that prevents the condition, and the reason the entry records a HIGH burden for something entirely avoidable. Guidance is directive: avoid valproate in people of childbearing potential where clinically feasible, and use lamotrigine, levetiracetam or oxcarbazepine instead. Timing is the whole of it. In Australian register data, malformation rates were 4.5% where valproate was reduced or withdrawn before pregnancy against 10.9% where it was unchanged, and 2.7% in the subgroup where it was stopped altogether. The cost falls on seizure control: in that same changed group — the 4.5% one, not the 2.7% subgroup — seizure-affected pregnancies rose from 31% to 46%. This is a trade, not a free improvement. Once a pregnancy has started the calculus reverses, and the guideline cautions against removing an effective drug.

evidence.reference_title: Teratogenesis, Perinatal, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes After In Utero Exposure to Antiseizure Medication: Practice Guideline From the AAN, AES, and SMFM.
evidence.snippet: Clinicians must avoid the use of valproic acid in PWECP to minimize the risk of MCMs or neural tube defects (NTDs), if clinically feasible.

evidence.reference_title: Teratogenesis, Perinatal, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes After In Utero Exposure to Antiseizure Medication: Practice Guideline From the AAN, AES, and SMFM.
evidence.snippet: Clinicians must consider using lamotrigine, levetiracetam, or oxcarbazepine in PWECP when appropriate based on the patient's epilepsy syndrome, likelihood of achieving seizure control, and comorbidities, to minimize the risk of MCMs.

evidence.reference_title: Pregnancy after valproate withdrawal-Fetal malformations and seizure control.
evidence.snippet: Although the available data have limitations, fetal malformation rates in the pregnancies studied were lower in the VPA changed pregnancies (4.5%) than in the VPA unchanged comparator pregnancies (10.9%, hazard ratio [HR] 0.412, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.190-0.892), and were only 2.7% where VPA intake was ceased before pregnancy

evidence.reference_title: Pregnancy after valproate withdrawal-Fetal malformations and seizure control.
evidence.snippet: Seizure-affected pregnancies were more frequent in the VPA changed pregnancies than in the VPA unchanged ones (46.2% vs 30.8%, HR 1.500, 95% CI 1.203-1.870).

evidence.reference_title: Teratogenesis, Perinatal, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes After In Utero Exposure to Antiseizure Medication: Practice Guideline From the AAN, AES, and SMFM.
evidence.snippet: Once a PWECP is already pregnant, clinicians should exercise caution in attempting to remove or replace an ASM that is effective in controlling generalized tonic-clonic or focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizures.

nodes.description: Valproate inhibits class I histone deacetylases, with HDAC1 inhibited at about 0.4 mM. The case that this is a teratogenic mechanism and not merely a pharmacological property rests on structure-activity evidence rather than on correlation: across twenty valproate derivatives, HDAC inhibitory potency tracks teratogenic potency, non-teratogenic analogues do not inhibit the enzyme, and a structurally unrelated HDAC inhibitor reproduces the malformations.

evidence.reference_title: Teratogenic effects mediated by inhibition of histone deacetylases: evidence from quantitative structure activity relationships of 20 valproic acid derivatives.
evidence.snippet: We also show a quantitative correlation between the IC50(HDAC) and the teratogenic potential of VPA derivatives, which clearly points toward HDACs as the formerly described teratogenic receptors of VPA-induced neural tube defects (NTDs).

evidence.reference_title: Teratogenic effects mediated by inhibition of histone deacetylases: evidence from quantitative structure activity relationships of 20 valproic acid derivatives.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that only VPA derivatives with a teratogenic potential in mice are able to induce a hyperacetylation in core histone H4 in teratocarcinoma F9 cells.

evidence.reference_title: Association of valproate-induced teratogenesis with histone deacetylase inhibition in vivo.
evidence.snippet: We found that VPA and other HDAC inhibitors cause very similar and characteristic developmental defects whereas VPA analogs with poor inhibitory activity in vivo have little teratogenic effect.

nodes.description: Cleft palate at about five times background odds, and specifically isolated cleft palate rather than cleft lip and palate — an eleven-fold increase for the isolated form against three-and-a-half-fold for cleft lip and palate. The distinction matters mechanistically as well as clinically, since the two have different embryology.

evidence.reference_title: In utero exposure to valproate increases the risk of isolated cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: Thirteen cases of OFC occurred in 1282 VPA monotherapy-exposed pregnancies in the UKEPR; nine had ICP and four had CLP, representing an 11.3-fold and 3.5-fold increase risk in ICP and CLP, respectively, over general population risk.

evidence.reference_title: Valproic acid monotherapy in pregnancy and major congenital malformations.
evidence.snippet: use of valproic acid monotherapy was associated with significantly increased risks for 6 of the 14 malformations under consideration; the adjusted odds ratios were as follows: spina bifida, 12.7 (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.7 to 20.7); atrial septal defect, 2.5 (95% CI, 1.4 to 4.4); cleft palate, 5.2 (95% CI, 2.8 to 9.9); hypospadias, 4.8 (95% CI, 2.9 to 8.1); polydactyly, 2.2 (95% CI, 1.0 to 4.5); and craniosynostosis, 6.8 (95% CI, 1.8 to 18.8).

nodes.description: The defining feature of the spectrum and the commonest one. Group studies of exposed children put the IQ deficit at 8-10 points; in individuals carrying a clinical diagnosis of the syndrome it is about 19 points, with a characteristic verbal-comprehension shortfall. The consensus statement makes the point that cognitive impairment is commoner than malformation, which is why it is curated as the leading phenotype and not as a complication of the malformations.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of individuals with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder; a consensus statement from the European Reference Network for Congenital Malformations and Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: There is replicated evidence of a reduction in IQ of 8–10 points compared to unexposed individuals and specific deficits in verbal skills

evidence.reference_title: Intellectual functioning in clinically confirmed fetal valproate syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Sixty one percent of cases demonstrated disproportionately lower verbal comprehension ability.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of individuals with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder; a consensus statement from the European Reference Network for Congenital Malformations and Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: The fact that the prevalence of the cognitive and neuropsychological deficits after VPA exposure is higher than that of the prevalence of VPA associated malformations suggests that an individual can demonstrate adverse effects of VPA exposure without necessarily having all of the physical features seen in FVS.

evidence.reference_title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes in children and adults with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder: A contribution from the ConcePTION project.
evidence.snippet: Individuals with a diagnosis of FVSD showed significantly higher levels of moderate (43.4%) and severe (14.4%) cognitive impairment than other groups (p = 0.003), high levels of required formal educational support (77.6%), and poorer academic competence than individuals not exposed to Valproate (p = 0.001).

nodes.description: The structural result in the face and skull: the recognizable gestalt, cleft palate — predominantly isolated rather than with cleft lip — and metopic suture ridging that at its extreme is craniosynostosis. Recorded as a tissue outcome rather than as a list of phenotypes so the crest mechanism has somewhere to land.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of individuals with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder; a consensus statement from the European Reference Network for Congenital Malformations and Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: The facial dysmorphism is characterised by a broad nasal bridge, short nose with forward-facing (anteverted) nostrils, small mouth with thin upper lip, everted lower lip flat philtrum, ridging of the metopic suture and neatly arched eyebrows

evidence.reference_title: In utero exposure to valproate increases the risk of isolated cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: ICP is the predominant cleft type seen in prenatal VPA exposure.

nodes.description: Premature suture fusion, metopic in the reported cases, at roughly seven times the background odds after first-trimester monotherapy.

evidence.reference_title: Valproic acid monotherapy in pregnancy and major congenital malformations.
evidence.snippet: use of valproic acid monotherapy was associated with significantly increased risks for 6 of the 14 malformations under consideration; the adjusted odds ratios were as follows: spina bifida, 12.7 (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.7 to 20.7); atrial septal defect, 2.5 (95% CI, 1.4 to 4.4); cleft palate, 5.2 (95% CI, 2.8 to 9.9); hypospadias, 4.8 (95% CI, 2.9 to 8.1); polydactyly, 2.2 (95% CI, 1.0 to 4.5); and craniosynostosis, 6.8 (95% CI, 1.8 to 18.8).

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of individuals with Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder; a consensus statement from the European Reference Network for Congenital Malformations and Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: The risk of cardiac malformations is increased 2–3 fold, that for cleft palate increased five-fold, that for craniosynostosis six-fold, and that for hypospadias and genitourinary (GU) malformations five-fold.

nodes.description: Speech delay is the single commonest reported problem in clinic series of fetal anticonvulsant syndrome, and language impairment persists beyond early childhood. It is prominent enough that MONDO's own definition singles out language and communication.

evidence.reference_title: A clinical study of 57 children with fetal anticonvulsant syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Forty four (77%) had learning difficulties, 46 (81%) had speech delay, 34 (60%) had gross motor delay, and 24 (42%) had fine motor delay.

evidence.reference_title: A clinical study of 57 children with fetal anticonvulsant syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Speech delay, joint laxity, glue ear, and myopia are common in the fetal anticonvulsant syndromes and autistic features and hyperactivity form part of the behavioural phenotype.

nodes.description: The design answers a question the clinical data pose but cannot settle: why exposure after organogenesis still harms neurodevelopment. By exposing human neurons at defined maturation stages it shows the damage is restricted to immature neurons, and identifies MARCKSL1 as the mediator downstream of HDAC and GSK-3 inhibition.
nodes.id: Directly reprogrammed human neurons with staged valproate exposure

nodes.description: The cortex is assembled with altered progenitor output: fewer outer radial glia in human organoids, excess superficial-layer projection neurons in mouse, and reduced Purkinje cell number in the rat cerebellum. The lamination and cell-number abnormalities are the tissue-level bridge between the progenitor disturbance and the behavioural outcome.

animal_models.description: The same exposure and timing reduce Purkinje cell number in the cerebellar vermis, with the posterior lobe affected more than the anterior — a regional gradient rather than a global loss.
animal_models.name: Prenatal valproate rat model of autism

evidence.reference_title: In Utero Exposure to Valproic Acid Induces Neocortical Dysgenesis via Dysregulation of Neural Progenitor Cell Proliferation/Differentiation.

nodes.description: In the exposed embryo the pattern of folate metabolites shifts, with formyl-tetrahydrofolates falling and tetrahydrofolate rising, attributed to inhibited transfer of the formyl group. The structure-activity argument applies on this branch as it does on the HDAC one: an analogue with antiepileptic activity but no teratogenic activity leaves embryonic folate metabolism alone. MTHFR is named here because the maternal 677C>T genotype modifies this branch's susceptibility, and the molecular function it reduces is what connects the gene to the metabolic disturbance: the knock-in mouse carrying that variant shows lower MTHFR enzymatic activity and raised homocysteine. The association and its limits are curated in the genetic section.

nodes.description: In the exposed embryo the acetylation mark rises within hours and is not uniform: it is concentrated in the neuroepithelium, heart and somites, which are the tissues that go on to malform. Other histone marks move with it while global DNA methylation does not, so the proximate lesion is chromatin state rather than methylation. In human neural progenitors the drug reaches two-thirds of all measured chromatin peaks, and — against the expectation for an HDAC inhibitor — closes more regions than it opens.

nodes.description: A population rather than a cell line, which is the point: with 83 genotyped donors the design can separate what the drug does in everyone from what it does only in some genetic backgrounds. Valproate remodelled two-thirds of measured chromatin peaks, reduced proliferation in every donor at a clinically relevant concentration, and shifted cells toward differentiation. Genetic variation modified the response at over a thousand loci, and a transcriptome-wide association in the valproate condition implicated folate metabolism genes in cognitive ability — which lands the two mechanistic branches curated here, chromatin and folate, in one human experiment.

nodes.description: Repair of the malformations as they arise: neural tube defect closure, cleft palate repair, hypospadias repair, cardiac repair, and craniofacial surgery for metopic synostosis. The craniosynostosis case is the one where timing has been argued to matter beyond the structural result — in the valproate-exposed trigonocephaly series, IQ was higher in those operated before six months, which is an observational association in a small series rather than a demonstrated cognitive benefit.

evidence.snippet: These patients' intelligence quotients (JQs) at the time of the most recent follow-up examination ranged from 45 to 100, with a mean of 75; IQs were significantly higher in patients who underwent surgery before reaching 6 months of age.
